pages.headline: India fourth-largest economy
pages.what: India overtook Japan to become the world's fourth-largest economy by nominal GDP in 2025, at USD 4.18 trillion. India was projected to overtake Germany in about 2.5 to 3 years. In PPP terms it is the third largest economy.
key: Nominal GDP 2025: USD 4.18 trillion, rank four, ahead of Japan
PPP rank: third
Per-capita GDP 2024: India USD 2,694, Japan USD 32,487
Projected to pass Germany in about 2.5 to 3 years
pages.static: Nominal GDP vs PPP; per-capita income as a development measure.
pages.angle: Equating a bigger economy with higher per-capita income.
pages.remember: Big economy, small per-capita: India fourth, Japan richer per head.

pages.headline: First Advance Estimates: 7.4% growth
pages.what: The National Statistics Office under MoSPI projected real GDP growth of 7.4 per cent for FY2025-26, against 6.5 per cent in FY2024-25. Real GVA is expected to grow 7.3 per cent and nominal GDP 8.0 per cent. A new GDP series is coming.
key: Real GVA growth: 7.3%; nominal GDP growth: 8.0%
Agriculture and allied: 3.1%; manufacturing and construction: 7.0%
Base year changing from 2011-12 to 2022-23
New series due February 2027
pages.static: National income accounting; GDP vs GVA; MoSPI and NSO.
pages.angle: Reversing the current-year and previous-year growth rates.
pages.remember: Seven-point-four now, six-point-five before.

pages.headline: Economic Survey 2025-26: growth outlook
pages.what: The Economic Survey 2025-26 estimated real GDP growth of 7.4 per cent for FY2025-26 and projected 6.8 to 7.2 per cent for FY2026-27. It called India the fastest-growing major economy for the fourth consecutive year.
key: FY2025-26 estimate: 7.4% (First Advance Estimate)
FY2026-27 projection: 6.8% to 7.2%
Medium-term potential growth: about 7%
Prepared by the Economic Division, DEA, under the Chief Economic Adviser
Fastest-growing major economy for the fourth year running
pages.static: Economic Survey as a pre-Budget document; role of the Chief Economic Adviser.
pages.angle: Taking the current-year estimate to be the next-year projection.
pages.remember: Survey: seven-point-four this year, 6.8 to 7.2 next.

pages.headline: Survey: record-low inflation, strong consumption
pages.what: The Economic Survey 2025-26 reported average CPI inflation of 1.7 per cent for April-December 2025, the lowest on record, against 4.6 per cent in 2024-25. Private final consumption was 61.5 per cent of GDP, the highest since 2011-12.
key: CPI inflation April-December 2025: 1.7%, lowest on record
Retail inflation 2024-25: 4.6%
Private final consumption: 61.5% of GDP, highest since 2011-12
Forex reserves: about USD 701.4 billion
Import cover: roughly 11 months
pages.static: CPI and inflation measurement; forex reserves and import cover.
pages.angle: Applying this year's low inflation figure to the earlier year.
pages.remember: Inflation 1.7 now, 4.6 before.

pages.headline: CAG publishes State Finances 2023-24
pages.what: The CAG released the second edition of its audited overview of State finances with a ten-year trend from 2014-15. It also flags unconditional cash transfers and rising guarantees as risks to State budgets.
key: Covers all 28 States; trend 2014-15 to 2023-24
Own tax revenue about 47% of revenue receipts; share in Union taxes 21.34% to 29.77%
16 States revenue surplus, 12 revenue deficit in 2023-24
18 States above 3% of GSDP fiscal deficit
Committed spending above half of revenue expenditure
pages.static: CAG (Article 148); Finance Commission devolution; FRBM limits.
pages.angle: Assuming States largely met the 3% limit.
pages.remember: CAG audit: 18 of 28 States over the 3% line.

pages.headline: New CPI series with base year 2024
pages.what: MoSPI released the Consumer Price Index on a new base year of 2024. January 2026 headline inflation was 2.75 per cent, and weights now come from the 2023-24 household expenditure survey.
key: Base 2024 replaces 2012; MoSPI compiles it
Weights: HCES 2023-24; basket 358 items; COICOP 2018
Rural housing index included for the first time
Food and beverages weight 36.75% (was 45.86%)
January 2026 inflation 2.75%; RBI target 4% plus or minus 2%
pages.static: Laspeyres index; RBI inflation targeting; CPI (Combined) as headline.
pages.angle: Attributing CPI to the RBI or Labour Bureau.
pages.remember: CPI 2024: MoSPI, 358 items, rural housing in.

pages.headline: PLFS December 2025: unemployment 4.8%
pages.what: The Periodic Labour Force Survey for December 2025 put India's labour force participation rate (15+) at 56.1 per cent and unemployment at 4.8 per cent. The worker population ratio was 53.4 per cent. Urban unemployment was far above rural.
key: Unemployment rate: 4.8%
Worker population ratio: 53.4%
Rural unemployment 3.9%; urban 6.7%
Urban female unemployment: 9.1%
pages.static: PLFS by MoSPI; LFPR, WPR and unemployment definitions.
pages.angle: Assuming rural unemployment is higher than urban.
pages.remember: Urban women face the highest jobless rate: 9.1%.

pages.headline: Tiger Global-Flipkart gains taxable
pages.what: The Supreme Court held that Tiger Global's 2018 sale of its Flipkart stake to Walmart, about USD 1.6 billion, is taxable in India. It denied India-Mauritius treaty benefits and set aside the Delhi High Court's 2024 judgment. The tax demand was nearly Rs 14,500 crore.
key: Deal: 2018 sale of Flipkart stake to Walmart (about USD 1.6 billion)
Treaty benefit under India-Mauritius DTAA denied
A Tax Residency Certificate alone does not guarantee treaty benefits
Reason: 'head and brain' outside Mauritius
Restored the 2020 Authority for Advance Rulings order; Delhi HC 2024 judgment set aside
pages.static: DTAA; General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR, effective 1 April 2017); treaty shopping.
pages.angle: Believing a Tax Residency Certificate is conclusive proof of treaty eligibility.
pages.remember: Paper residency fails if the brain sits elsewhere.

pages.headline: RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026
pages.what: The RBI unveiled the Reserve Bank Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026, replacing the 2021 scheme from 1 July 2026. It raises the compensation a customer can claim and covers banks, RRBs, urban cooperative banks, deposit-taking NBFCs and prepaid payment issuers.
key: In force from 1 July 2026; replaces 2021 scheme
Compensation: up to Rs 30 lakh for consequential financial loss
Up to Rs 3 lakh for non-financial loss
Approach regulated entity first; Ombudsman after 30 days
Appeal to RBI Executive Director within 30 days
pages.static: RBI's consumer protection role; Banking Ombudsman schemes.
pages.angle: Swapping the Rs 30 lakh and Rs 3 lakh limits.
pages.remember: Thirty lakh for money lost, three lakh for distress.

pages.headline: RBI proposes reopening UCB licensing
pages.what: The RBI proposed resuming the licensing of new Urban Cooperative Banks after nearly two decades, with fresh eligibility norms. UCBs are regulated by the RBI for banking functions, while State Governments or the Central Registrar handle registration and management.
key: Proposal: resume new UCB licences after nearly two decades
Banking Regulation Act, 1949: Sections 22 and 23 on licensing
Dual regulation: RBI (banking) and Registrar (management)
First urban credit society: Anyonya Sahakari Mandali, Baroda, 1889
pages.static: Cooperative banking; dual control; Banking Regulation Act (as applicable to cooperatives).
pages.angle: Forgetting the dual control of UCBs.
pages.remember: UCBs: RBI for banking, Registrar for management.

pages.headline: PFRDA forms Sahoo and SAARG committees
pages.what: PFRDA set up a 15-member committee headed by M.S. Sahoo to design a framework for assured payouts under the NPS. It also constituted the nine-member SAARG Committee chaired by Narayan Ramachandran to modernise NPS investment guidelines.
key: Sahoo committee: 15 members; assured-payout framework
Sahoo is a former IBBI chairperson
Remit: lock-in, pricing, risk, capital norms, tax treatment
SAARG Committee: nine members, chaired by Narayan Ramachandran
SAARG: investment framework review; nine months to report
pages.static: National Pension System; PFRDA Act, 2013.
pages.angle: Mixing up which committee handles payouts and which handles investments.
pages.remember: Sahoo for payouts; SAARG for portfolios.

pages.headline: PFRDA issues NPS Vatsalya guidelines
pages.what: PFRDA issued the NPS Vatsalya Scheme Guidelines 2025 for a contributory pension scheme for minors. The account is held in the minor's name and run by a guardian, with a minimum yearly contribution of Rs 250.
key: Minimum Rs 250 per year; no maximum
Account in minor's name, operated by guardian
Partial withdrawal: up to 25% of own contributions after three years
Purposes: education, medical treatment, specified disabilities
NRIs and OCIs below 18 are eligible
pages.static: Pension reforms; role of PFRDA.
pages.angle: Assuming NRI and OCI minors are excluded.
pages.remember: Rs 250 a year starts a child's pension.

pages.headline: LRS remittances hit two-year low
pages.what: Outward remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme fell to a two-year low of USD 1.94 billion in November 2025, driven by lower spending on foreign education. The scheme lets resident individuals send money abroad within a yearly limit.
key: Remittances: USD 1.94 billion in November 2025, two-year low
Driver: lower foreign-education spending
LRS introduced 4 February 2004 under FEMA, 1999
Limit: USD 250,000 per financial year
TCS applies on remittances above Rs 7 lakh
pages.static: FEMA, 1999 (current vs capital account transactions).
pages.angle: Linking LRS to the Banking Regulation Act instead of FEMA.
pages.remember: LRS is a FEMA scheme with a USD 250,000 cap.

pages.headline: RBI overhauls priority sector lending norms
pages.what: The RBI's 2025 Directions revised PSL targets and classification. Small Finance Banks get a lower target, NCDC on-lending is recognised, and external auditors must certify PSL claims.
key: SFB target: 75% down to 60% of ANBC
Domestic commercial banks: 40% of ANBC or CEOBE, whichever is higher
Regional Rural Banks: 75% of ANBC
Bank loans to NCDC for on-lending qualify as PSL
External audit certification to avoid double counting
pages.static: Priority sector lending; Adjusted Net Bank Credit; co-lending.
pages.angle: Mixing up the 40% bank target with the 75% RRB target.
pages.remember: PSL: banks 40, RRBs 75, SFBs now 60.

pages.headline: FDI up 18% in H1 FY26
pages.what: DPIIT data showed FDI inflows of USD 35.2 billion in April-September 2025, up 18 per cent from USD 29.8 billion a year before. Singapore, the US and Mauritius were the top sources, and Maharashtra took about 30 per cent of inflows.
key: H1 FY26 FDI: USD 35.2 billion (up 18%)
Year-earlier: USD 29.8 billion
Cumulative since April 2000: USD 1.12 trillion
Top sources: Singapore (about USD 12 billion), US, Mauritius
Top States: Maharashtra (about 30%), Karnataka, Tamil Nadu
pages.static: FDI routes and sectors; DPIIT as nodal body for FDI data.
pages.angle: Naming Mauritius as the top source.
pages.remember: Singapore leads, Maharashtra gets a third.

pages.headline: NITI Aayog releases EPI 2024
pages.what: NITI Aayog released the fourth edition of the Export Preparedness Index (EPI 2024). Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh topped the Large States. Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Nagaland, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, and Goa led other categories.
key: Top Large States: Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, UP, Andhra Pradesh
Small States, NE States and UTs top: Uttarakhand, J&K, Nagaland, DNH&DD, Goa
Four pillars, 13 sub-pillars, 70 indicators
Business Ecosystem 40%; other three pillars 20% each
First edition published in 2020
pages.static: NITI Aayog indices; export promotion.
pages.angle: Placing Karnataka in the top Large States.
pages.remember: Business Ecosystem gets forty; the rest twenty each.

pages.headline: A decade of Startup India
pages.what: National Startup Day marked ten years since Startup India was launched on 16 January 2016. January 16 was declared National Startup Day in 2022. The initiative offers funding, mentoring and tax support.
key: Launched 16 Jan 2016; National Startup Day since 2022
Startup: up to 10 years old, turnover up to Rs 200 crore
Deep tech: up to 20 years, turnover up to Rs 300 crore
Fund of Funds Rs 10,000 crore via SIDBI; Seed Fund Scheme Rs 945 crore
Credit Guarantee Scheme through NCGTC; MAARG mentorship portal
pages.static: DPIIT recognition; Atal Innovation Mission; NIDHI.
pages.angle: Using the 10-year and Rs 200 crore limits for deep tech.
pages.remember: Startup 10/200; deep tech 20/300.

pages.headline: NITI Aayog report on MSME scheme convergence
pages.what: NITI Aayog's report proposes converging more than 18 MSME schemes through information convergence and process convergence. It suggests merging SFURTI with MSE-CDP. The Udyam portal has 3.94 crore registered MSMEs.
key: Author: NITI Aayog
More than 18 MSME schemes to be converged
Two routes: information convergence and process convergence
Merge SFURTI with MSE-CDP
Udyam registrations: 3.94 crore; MSMEs 27-30% of GDP
pages.static: MSME classification; Udyam registration.
pages.angle: Crediting the report to the Ministry of MSME.
pages.remember: NITI Aayog merges SFURTI with MSE-CDP.

pages.headline: Cabinet approves Rs 5,000 crore for SIDBI
pages.what: The Union Cabinet approved equity infusion of Rs 5,000 crore into SIDBI over three years to expand MSME credit. SIDBI is the apex MSME financing institution. MSME beneficiaries are projected to rise from 76.26 lakh in FY25 to about 102 lakh by FY28.
key: Equity infusion: Rs 5,000 crore over three years
SIDBI Act, 1989
Headquarters: Lucknow
Beneficiaries: 76.26 lakh (FY25) to about 102 lakh (FY28)
Also manages the Rs 10,000 crore Fund of Funds for Startups
pages.static: Development financial institutions; MSME credit.
pages.angle: Placing SIDBI's headquarters in Mumbai.
pages.remember: SIDBI sits in Lucknow.

pages.headline: Design Linked Incentive scheme for chips
pages.what: MeitY's Design Linked Incentive scheme under the Semicon India Programme offers up to 50 per cent of eligible design expenditure and a sales-linked incentive. It had sanctioned 24 chip-design projects. C-DAC is the nodal agency and runs the ChipIN Centre.
key: Design support: up to 50%, capped at Rs 15 crore per application
Sales incentive: 4-6% of net sales for five years, capped at Rs 30 crore
24 chip-design projects sanctioned
Semicon India Programme outlay: Rs 76,000 crore
Nodal agency: C-DAC; ChipIN Centre serves about 1 lakh engineers
pages.static: Semiconductor mission; MeitY.
pages.angle: Swapping the Rs 15 crore and Rs 30 crore caps.
pages.remember: Fifteen crore for design, thirty crore for sales.

pages.headline: Five firms selected under PLI for white goods
pages.what: Five companies were selected under the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for White Goods, which covers air conditioners and LED lights. The incentive is 4 to 6 per cent of incremental sales for five years.
key: Products: air conditioners and LED lights
Incentive: 4-6% on incremental sales for five years
Period: FY2021-22 to FY2028-29
Nodal body: DPIIT
Base year for incremental turnover: 2019-20
pages.static: PLI schemes and Atmanirbhar Bharat.
pages.angle: Adding refrigerators or washing machines to the covered products.
pages.remember: White-goods PLI covers ACs and LEDs only.

pages.headline: Tex-RAMPS MoUs signed with 15 States
pages.what: At the National Textile Ministers' Conference in Guwahati, the Ministry of Textiles signed MoUs with 15 States for Tex-RAMPS. The scheme is fully centrally funded and runs from FY2025-26 to FY2030-31, aiming at a USD 350 billion textile industry.
key: MoUs with 15 States at Guwahati
Fully centrally funded
Period: FY2025-26 to FY2030-31
Rs 12 lakh per State/UT per year
Rs 1 lakh per district per year
pages.static: Centrally sponsored vs Central Sector schemes; textile policy.
pages.angle: Swapping the State and district amounts.
pages.remember: Twelve lakh a State, one lakh a district.

pages.headline: India is world's largest rice producer
pages.what: Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said India's rice production reached 150.18 million tonnes, ahead of China's 145.28 million tonnes. India supplies about 40 per cent of global rice exports, with shipments above 20 million tonnes.
key: India 150.18 mt vs China 145.28 mt
About 40% of global rice exports; above 20 million tonnes
Primarily a Kharif crop
Needs about 150 cm rainfall and 25-35 degrees Celsius
pages.static: Cropping seasons; rice in the Indian agriculture syllabus.
pages.angle: Calling rice a rabi crop.
pages.remember: Rice is Kharif; India now tops China.

pages.headline: Milk output at 247.87 million tonnes
pages.what: India's milk production reached 247.87 million tonnes in 2024-25, up 3.58 per cent from 239.30 million tonnes in 2023-24. Uttar Pradesh was the largest producer with 15.66 per cent. India has been the world's largest milk producer since 1998.
key: 247.87 million tonnes in 2024-25 (up 3.58%)
Top State: Uttar Pradesh, 15.66%
World's largest producer since 1998
Operation Flood: 13 January 1970, NDDB, Verghese Kurien
White Revolution 2.0: Ministry of Cooperation, 19 September 2024
pages.static: Operation Flood; cooperative dairying (Amul).
pages.angle: Giving the wrong ministry for White Revolution 2.0.
pages.remember: White Revolution 2.0 belongs to Cooperation.

pages.headline: Coking coal added to critical and strategic minerals
pages.what: The Government added coking coal to Part D of the First Schedule of the MMDR Act. The move recognises its role in blast-furnace steelmaking and aims to cut import dependence.
key: Part D of First Schedule, MMDR Act 1957: critical and strategic minerals
About 95% of the steel sector's coking coal is imported
Reserves about 37.37 billion tonnes, mainly Jharkhand
Used in steel (blast furnace), cement, chemicals
MMDR Act also created District Mineral Foundations and NMET
pages.static: MMDR Act, 1957 and 2023 amendment on critical minerals; National Critical Mineral Mission.
pages.angle: Placing coking coal reserves in the west.
pages.remember: Coking coal: critical mineral now, Jharkhand-heavy.
